# Didache Chapter 11 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 11

---

## Chapter 11

**1** Receive anyone who comes and teaches you all the things stated above.

**2** But if a teacher turns aside and teaches a different doctrine that undermines what was stated above, do not listen to him. However, if his teaching promotes greater righteousness and knowledge of the Lord, receive him as you would the Lord.

**3** Concerning apostles and prophets: follow the rule of the Gospel.

**4** Welcome every apostle who comes to you as you would welcome the Lord.

**5** But he is not to stay more than one day; if necessary, two days. If he stays three days, he is a false prophet.

**6** When the apostle leaves, he is to take only enough bread to last until his next destination. If he asks for money, he is a false prophet.

**7** Do not test or pass judgment on any prophet who speaks in the Spirit — for every sin shall be forgiven, but this sin shall not be forgiven.

**8** Not everyone who speaks in the Spirit is a prophet — only the one whose conduct is in keeping with the Lord. By their conduct, the false prophet and the true prophet are to be distinguished.

**9** Any prophet who in the Spirit commands a meal to be set shall not eat from it himself; if he does eat from it, he is a false prophet.

**10** Every prophet who teaches the truth — if he does not practice what he teaches, he is a false prophet.

**11** But as for a proven prophet who enacts the worldly mystery of the Church — do not judge him, provided he does not teach others to do the same. His judgment belongs to God, for the ancient prophets acted in this way as well.

**12** If anyone says in the Spirit, "Give me money" — or anything else — do not listen to him. But if he directs that gifts be given to others in need, no one is to judge him.

---

### Council Notes

**On v.7 (blasphemy against the Spirit):** All three agents recognize that this verse echoes the Blasphemy against the Holy Spirit saying (Matt 12:31-32). The community has been taught not to test genuine prophetic speech — to do so is equivalent to attributing the Spirit's work to evil. This is placed very practically: it protects genuine prophets from community dismissal.

**On v.9 ("orders a meal in the Spirit"):** EMET's "orders a table" is more literal (τράπεζαν); LOGOS's "commands a meal to be set" is clearer. SOPHIA adopts LOGOS. The prohibition on the prophet eating the meal they requested is a test of disinterested prophecy.

**On v.11 (μυστήριον κοσμικὸν ἐκκλησίας — "worldly mystery of the Church"):** This is the most debated verse in the Didache. Possible interpretations: (a) a prophet who takes a spiritual spouse for symbolic purposes (like Hosea); (b) a prophet who enacts the relationship between Christ and the Church in their own marriage. The key ruling from all agents: do not attempt to resolve the interpretive debate in the translation. Render literally and note the ambiguity.
**Ruling:** "Enacts the worldly mystery of the Church" retained. The council notes that κοσμικόν here likely does not mean "worldly" in a pejorative sense but rather "pertaining to this age/this realm" (as opposed to the heavenly). A translator note explains the interpretive range.

**On v.12 (money requests):** All agents agree: requesting money for oneself is disqualifying; directing the community to give to the poor is legitimate. The distinction is the direction of the gift.
